extracted.intended_audience: International Searching Authority examiners, other patent office examiners and applicants preparing/responding to PCT international search reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, completing and assessing the PCT international search report (Form PCT/ISA/210), including how to handle titles, abstracts, drawings, classification, searches, citations and reporting of limitations or special searches. Primarily directed to examiners but also describes applicant rights and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing handling and indication
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing was furnished as part of the international application or subsequently for the purposes of international search, item 1 indicates whether it was filed as part of the international application or subsequently, and whether it was accompanied by a statement that the sequence listing does not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. If the applicant failed to furnish a sequence listing complying with the relevant standard in an accepted language and the search was carried out without the sequence listing, this fact is indicated in item 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Box 1.c of the first sheet when there are defined nucleotides or four or more specifically defined amino acids; use Box No. I on continuation sheet. See paragraphs 4.15 and 15.12 for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to main international search report in supplementary searches
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of supplementary international search reports, item 1.d of the first sheet indicates whether the international search report was received in time to take it into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the international search report was not taken into account, include an indication of any assumptions made as to the scope of the main international search in the Annex of Form PCT/SISA/501 concerning the scope of the supplementary international search (see paragraph 15.93).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate restriction of subject of international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must indicate whether the search was restricted or not and, if restrictions are applied, identify the claims not searched and the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four categories of restriction: (i) subject matter not required to be searched by the International Authority; (ii) claims for which a meaningful search cannot be carried out; (iii) multiple dependent claims not complying with Rule 6.4(a); (iv) lack of unity of invention. The written opinion will also report relevant facts, possibly by reference to the full explanation in the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxing for claims not searched (reasons (i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims are not searched for reasons (i) to (iii), box 2 of the first sheet of the international search report is checked and Box No. II on continuation sheet is completed giving details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the claims not searched and state the specific reason(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of omnibus claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims which rely on references to the description or drawings (omnibus claims) are searched and reported upon if they can be given a definite construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omnibus claims breach Rule 6.2(a) (no reference to the description or drawings except when absolutely necessary), this may be reported in Box No. VII of the written opinion or report for international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependent claims and national law exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If the national law of the Office acting as ISA permits multiple dependent claims which do not comply with Rule 6.4(a), such claims are included in the international search and no indication is made under item 3 of Box No. II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow national law as to multiple dependent claims when preparing the international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting lack of unity (box 3 and Box No. III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where lack of unity has been found, check box 3 of the first sheet and complete Box No. III on continuation sheet irrespective of whether an invitation to pay additional search fees has issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the separate inventions present, whether additional search fees were requested and paid, which claims were searched, and whether additional fees were accompanied by a protest. For supplementary international searches, only a single invention is searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirement: short and precise
rubrics_metrics.description: The title must be short and precise (preferably from two to seven words in English or when translated into English) and should clearly and concisely state the technical designation of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal names, trade names or non-technical terms; do not use 'etc.'; avoid vague single-word titles like 'Method', 'Apparatus', 'Chemical Compounds' that do not state the technical designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner to draft title when missing or deficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is required to draft a title where the applicant has not responded to an invitation to provide a title, no title was filed and receiving Office omitted to invite correction, or the title is deficient under Rule 4.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner need not obtain applicant approval; establish the title by completion of item 4 of the first sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract is required and for technical information only
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is merely for use as technical information and must not be used for interpreting the scope of protection sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft so it assists scientists/engineers/researchers in searching; make it possible to assess whether the full application should be consulted; see WIPO Standard ST.12/A for abstract preparation guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content: summary of disclosure and technical field
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should provide a summary of the disclosure as contained in the description, claims and drawings, indicate the technical field, clearly state the technical problem, the gist of the solution, and the principal use(s) of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft as an efficient scanning tool for searching purposes; each main technical feature mentioned and illustrated by a drawing should be followed by its reference sign in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be as concise as the disclosure permits (preferably 50 to 150 words if in English or translated into English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lengthy abstracts and unnecessary words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract must not contain statements of merits or speculative application
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should not contain statements on the alleged merits or value of the claimed invention or on its speculative application; avoid phrases which can be implied, e.g., 'This disclosure concerns', or 'This invention relates to'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove promotional or speculative language; focus on technical facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract clarity and reference numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be clear and easy to understand. Reference numerals used in the abstract must correspond to those in the figures; absence of reference numerals on figures must be accepted as examiner cannot initiate their inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coherence between abstract and drawings; include reference signs for main features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner to amend or establish abstract when missing or non-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: If no abstract is filed, or the abstract does not comply with Rule 8, the ISA establishes or amends the abstract to bring it into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend abstract where it is overly lengthy without justification, contains statements of merits/speculation, or fails to indicate the gist of the solution. Review should be completed in parallel so as not to impact search completion date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant comment period on examiner-established abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is allowed one month from the mailing date of the ISR to submit proposed modifications or comments on the abstract established by the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner shall consider proposed modifications/comments and decide whether to modify the abstract. If the ISA modifies the abstract, it notifies the International Bureau and applicant using Form PCT/ISA/205; the examiner need not reply to comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure selection for abstract publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Where drawings exist, the applicant should suggest a figure to accompany the abstract. If none is suggested or suggested figure is not best, the examiner should select the figure that best characterizes the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally select only one figure; include more than one only in exceptional circumstances. Avoid figures with significant text; if no useful figure exists, indicate none. Indicate choice under item 6 of first sheet; change wording if multiple figures are selected (singular to plural).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligatory IPC classification assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA assigns obligatory 'invention information' IPC symbols in accordance with the Guide to the IPC and records them in Box A of the second sheet of the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the edition of the IPC in force at the time; non-obligatory IPC symbols (optional indexing codes) need not be applied. No additional classification during supplementary searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields searched to be listed
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR lists the classification identification of the fields searched in Box B of the second sheet; indicate which classification system was used if not IPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record IPC symbols when used for the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation of minimum documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA consults the minimum documentation specified in Rule 34 and considers other relevant databases or search resources as listed in Search Guidance IPDL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When IPC classification terms were searched, the examiner should enter associated IPC symbols on the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify documentation searched other than minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documentation other than the PCT minimum documentation is searched, identify such documentation in Box B of the second sheet when practicable (used for non-electronic databases, paper or microfilm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given (e.g., 'CAPRI: IPC F16B 1/02', national classification codes). For supplementary searches, scope may assume main minimum documentation included in the main ISR; an extra sheet may be used for longer comments on scope and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate third-party observation sources when relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner cites a document listed in a third party observation which would not have been found in the documentation searched, he may indicate 'Third party observation submitted [Date]' in the 'documentation searched other than the minimum documentation' box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides traceability that the citation originated from a third-party observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic database identification and search query reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an electronic database is used, the name of the database may be included; depending on policy, examiners may indicate exact search queries used, or a summary of queries if exact queries are impractical to record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including exact query/history may help national examiners fully interpret and rely upon the international search; see paragraph 15.62 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords reporting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Where keywords (search terms) are used, it may be useful to include the keywords on the ISR. If many keywords, include a representative sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Keywords: A, B, C, and similar terms'. Merely putting 'keywords searched' without specifying actual keywords is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and sequence search reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure searches are not conveniently indicated but can be noted descriptively (e.g., 'structure search carried out based on the quinoline nucleus in formula (I)'). Sequence searches should be dealt with similarly (e.g., 'search of SEQ ID 1-5' or indicate nucleic acid sequence and region searched).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching a particular region of a longer referenced sequence, indicate the region, e.g., 'search of SEQ ID NO: 1 for nucleotides 1150-1250 only.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No need to indicate means of database access
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no need to indicate the way a database was accessed (for example, via the Internet or via a particular service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the database and queries/keywords rather than access method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify relevant previous searches consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISR is partly or wholly based on a previous search for a similar subject, identify the previous application number and relevant search history consulted where appropriate, or include a summary if full details cannot be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the previous application is unpublished but the applicant is the same, the information may be sent informally to the applicant when the ISR is transmitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of 'documents considered to be relevant' entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of Box C has three components: the citation category; the citation of the document together with identification of relevant passages where appropriate; and identification of relevant claim numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These components should be provided for each cited document and are discussed in paragraphs 16.65–16.80.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection principle for cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents selected for citation should be the prior art that is closest to the applicant’s invention; duplication of teachings by citation of multiple documents showing same inventive elements should be minimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which portions/pages of a document are most relevant; for non-English patent documents, preferably also indicate corresponding part of English family member (but do not cite English member as separate document). Consider putting this info in the patent family annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary search citation restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: In supplementary international searches, the examiner need not include citations of documents already cited in the main ISR except where needed in conjunction with new documents (e.g., to form a Y combination) or where the main ISR clearly failed to recognize a document's relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary inclusion and reassessment; include cited main-ISR documents only when necessary (e.g., to cite as category 'Y').

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category must be indicated for each document
rubrics_metrics.description: A category (alphabetic character) must always be indicated for each cited document, combinations of categories are possible where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories per Administrative Instructions: define relevance (see following specific categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category X – particularly relevant document alone prejudices novelty/inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'X' applies where a document, taken alone, means a claimed invention cannot be considered novel or, when considered with common general knowledge, cannot be considered to involve an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark X where the document alone attacks novelty or inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Y – combined documents prejudice inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'Y' applies where a document cannot be considered to involve an inventive step only when combined with one or more other documents of the same category, such combination being obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Y where combination with other Y documents leads to lack of inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A – state of the art not prejudicing novelty or inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'A' applies where a cited document represents state of the art not prejudicial to the novelty or inventive step of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A for background or relevant art that doesn't attack novelty/inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category O – non-written disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'O' denotes citations referring to non-written disclosures (e.g., conference proceedings) and is always accompanied by a symbol indicating relevance (O,X; O,Y; or O,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details of the non-written disclosure and, where appropriate, any related written references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category P – intermediate documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'P' denotes documents published on dates between the application filing date and the priority date (or on the very day of earliest priority); P is accompanied by relevance symbol (P,X; P,Y; or P,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when publication date lies between priority and filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category T – documents relating to theory or principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'T' is used where a document published after the filing or priority date is not in conflict with the application but is useful for better understanding the principle/theory underlying the invention or to show reasoning/facts underlying the invention are incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for supporting or contextual references published later than priority/filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category E – potentially conflicting patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'E' applies to patent documents bearing a filing or priority date earlier than the filing date of the application being searched but published on or after the international filing date and whose content would constitute prior art relevant to novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E may be accompanied by X, Y, or A for Offices that allow combination of E documents for inventive step purposes. Exception for patent documents based on the priority under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D – documents cited in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'D' denotes documents already cited in the description of the patent application; D is accompanied by relevance symbol (D,X; D,Y; or D,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates examiner is citing documents the applicant already mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category L – documents cited for other reasons (evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'L' is for documents cited for reasons other than relevance to novelty/inventive step/state of the art, e.g., to cast doubt on priority or to establish publication date of another citation; brief reasons should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: L documents need not be indicated as relevant to particular claims unless the evidence relates only to certain claims—in which case, indicate those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial pre-PCT disclosures and applicant declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain cases the invention may have been disclosed before the relevant PCT date in a manner excluded from state of the art under national law; applicants may declare such excluded state of the art in the request form according to Rule 4.17(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exemptions do not necessarily apply in all designated States and the documents must still be cited on the ISR with appropriate category and may be considered in the written opinion and during international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between documents and claims (claim mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each citation should include a reference to the claims to which it relates; different relevant parts of a cited document should each be related to claims similarly, and the same document may represent different categories with respect to different claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where necessary, relate specific parts/passages of the cited document to specific claim numbers; exception: 'L' documents and 'A' documents guidance noted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for patent documents per WIPO ST.14
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of patent documents should include: issuing office two-letter code, document number as given by office, kind of document (WIPO ST.16), name of patentee/applicant (caps), date of publication (YYYY), and indications of location of most relevant material (paragraph/page/line numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple renderings exist (PDF, HTML) it may be necessary to indicate which version is referred to. WIPO ST.14 gives recommendations for identifying passages where paragraph/page/line numbers are not well defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for articles/serial publications per WIPO ST.14
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of an article should include: author name(s) (caps), title of the article (abbreviated or truncated as appropriate), title of periodical (abbreviations per practice allowed), location within the serial (date/year/month/day where available, issue, pagination), and standard identifier if available (ISBN/ISSN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include relevant passages or figures of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English non-patent literature citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-patent literature citations in a language other than English, include the original reference where technically possible, followed by an official English translation in round brackets if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no official translation exists for some elements, an informal translation may be provided after the original elements and preceded by 'non-official translation'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of oral disclosures, uses, exhibitions and other non-written means
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of an oral disclosure/use/exhibition/non-written making-available should be made according to ST.14 indicating the earliest date of disclosure to the public, applying the provisions of ST.2 for year/month/day where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include later relevant dates (e.g., publication of proceedings, internet posting) and retrieval dates for internet citations. For audio/video, indicate specific timeline sections if relevant (e.g., 'from 01:22 to 01:56'). Preferably provide details of the earlier disclosure first, followed by the document that refers to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide examples and exemplar citation formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Use provided examples (conference proceedings, reports) as models for citing complex situations where non-written disclosures are later published or reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow example formats given in WIPO ST.14 and paragraph 16.78D when citing such documents to ensure clarity and retrievability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of search report boxes for title/abstract/figure amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner indicates approval or amendment of title, abstract text, and the selection of the figure to accompany the abstract in items 4 to 6 of the first sheet; Box No. IV is used to record any new or amended abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure does not apply to supplementary international searches; for international-type searches the agreement between ISA and national Office determines review of title/abstract.
